rationale: The question has two parts that no single design answers: how often and in whom line complications occur (a record-based quantitative strand over 1,870 existing episodes), and why they occur at home in ways the records do not show (interviews with patients, carers and agency nurses). An explanatory sequential mixed methods design runs the cohort first and samples interviews from its extremes, as in the retrieved study that changed a similar service's priorities (c3). Complications are common enough for the cohort (c1), vary by nursing team (c2), and are partly invisible in hospital records (c4), and patients delay reporting (c5), which only interviews can explain.
alternatives: Retrospective record review alone (refused: it cannot see home-managed problems or explain delays in reporting)
Interviews alone (refused: without the cohort there is no way to choose whom to interview or to size the problem)
Prospective cohort with standardised line assessments at every visit (refused: needs agency cooperation and funding not yet available)
whyNotMoreComplex: A prospective multi-agency cohort or a trial of line types would answer narrower questions at far higher cost; the service first needs to know where to act, which the existing records plus targeted interviews can show.

decision.statement: Run an explanatory sequential mixed methods study: a record-based cohort of OPAT episodes from 2021 to 2025 linked to emergency visits and vascular access records, followed by interviews with patients, carers and agency nurses sampled from the extremes of the cohort results.
decision.question: Which design will show where the OPAT service should act first to reduce line complications?

criteria.text: Line complications are common and vary by care arrangement, so explaining them can direct the first intervention.
Home-managed complications cannot be counted without the agency's visit notes.

gates.requirement: Home infusion agency agreement to share nursing visit notes for OPAT patients
Research ethics board approval for linked record review and interviews
Protected fellow time for data extraction and interviews
gates.evidence: Investigator constraint: about 60 hours of an infectious diseases fellow's time over six months

decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1 to c5 from retrieved records. The agency data-sharing gate has no evidence and stays unknown; the ethics gate waits for the board meeting of 2026-10-14.

summary: Explanatory sequential mixed methods recommended; the decision rests on five ledger claims and is blocked by two unknown gates, one of them the agency's data sharing.
